description:
The iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch revolutionized how people live, communicate, and connect. Come help transform how more than a billion people make their personal devices uniquely theirs!
We’re looking for a creative, customer-focused, technical engineer to help us create Widgets, Live Activities, and Controls experience. 

Our team (iOS System Spaces) is responsible for a significant portion of the iOS system experience including Lock Screen, Wallpapers, StandBy, Home Screen, Notifications, and Control Center! Come work with a fantastic team of engineers, world class designers, and an incredibly strong set of peers to deliver the best mobile experience on the planet!


Description
You will work with the team at the forefront of personal customization for the most popular software platforms to ever exist. 
Widgets, Live Activities and Controls are a critical component of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS. 
Our team is responsible for the infrastructure that powers them. 
If you’re not *exceedingly* passionate about building the best mobile experience, this role is not right for you!

Our team is here to make a difference. To “put a ding in the universe,” and that’s not easy. You’ll be expected to push the envelope and to ship compelling designs at the very edge of what’s technically possible. You’ll have a voice in the room as critical decisions are made that will affect, impact, and improve the day-to-day lives of countless individuals.

Minimum qualifications
BS in Computer Science or equivalent preferred.
Deep understanding of modern software development methodologies, architecture, and design
Experience developing with UIKIT, SWIFTUI, or other application frameworks
Open-Minded with strong Collaboration skills
^ Not kidding about this, you will be learning constantly and collaborating extensively with peer teams, designers, teams across apple, and senior leaders

Preferred qualifications
Strong problem solving, critical thinking, and communication skills
Ability to think laterally and ask incisive (and sometimes foolish) questions
